subject: astronomy_astrophysics

resources.title: Introduction to Astronomy
resources.notes: Quantitative introduction requiring no prior astronomy knowledge; includes problem sets, solutions and exams. Covers planets, telescopes, stars, galaxies, compact objects and cosmology.

resources.title: The Solar System
resources.notes: Undergraduate planetary-science course with problem sets and explicit celestial-mechanics, planetary-formation, atmospheres, surfaces and exploration material.

resources.title: Modern Astrophysics
resources.notes: Physics-based astrophysics course with problem sets and exams covering stellar structure, compact objects, interstellar medium, galaxies and cosmology.

resources.title: Astrophysics I
resources.notes: Graduate introduction spanning stellar structure/evolution, galactic dynamics and dark matter with assigned problem sets.

resources.title: Hands-On Astronomy: Observing Stars and Planets
resources.notes: Hands-on telescope, imaging, spectroscopy, astronomical computing and data-processing course. Physical observing competence still requires actual equipment/practice beyond catalog ingestion.

resources.title: NASA Astrophysics Data Centers
resources.notes: NASA directory for HEASARC, IRSA, MAST, ADS and other astrophysics data systems; use archive-specific identifiers and provenance.

resources.title: High Energy Astrophysics Science Archive Research Center (HEASARC)
resources.notes: NASA-designated multi-mission archive for EUV, X-ray, gamma-ray and CMB astronomy with data-access APIs and analysis tools.

resources.title: NASA Astrophysics Data System (ADS)
resources.notes: Literature discovery and bibliographic infrastructure; linked article rights must be verified item by item.

resources.title: Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST)
resources.notes: NASA-funded archive focused on optical, ultraviolet and near-infrared astronomical datasets, including major space-telescope missions.

coverage_notes: Mappings use only finalized astronomy_astrophysics taxonomy keys already present in this manifest.
MIT 8.282J supplies a genuine beginner-to-undergraduate instructional bridge; it is not labeled foundation because its mathematics/physics prerequisites exceed a true foundation course.

The Solar System provides explicit celestial-mechanics instruction, but celestial_mechanics is not added as a subsubject because that key was not present in the fetched finalized manifest; taxonomy must be verified before introducing a new key.
Dedicated foundation-level astronomy remains a measured gap.
Gravitational astrophysics remains conservatively mapped through literature discovery rather than overstating course/archive coverage.

Research archives and bibliographic systems are evidence infrastructure, not proof of expert readiness; expert competence still requires assessed research, analysis, reproducibility and validation evidence.
